items.t: Said Interior is committed to unlocking energy dominance "to make life more affordable for every American family."
items.q: unlock America’s full potential in energy dominance and economic development to make life more affordable for every American family

items.t: Signed a bill exempting military pay from state income tax for active duty, National Guard and Reserve members in North Dakota.
items.q: Gov. Doug Burgum today signed a bill that exempts military pay from state income tax for active duty, National Guard and Reserve members

items.t: Signed Senate Bill 2351, which exempts Social Security income from North Dakota state income tax.
items.q: Burgum also signed Senate Bill 2351, which exempts Social Security income from state income tax, becoming the 38th state to do so.

items.t: Said "securing our border and protecting our nation’s resources go hand in hand."
items.q: Securing our border and protecting our nation’s resources go hand in hand

items.t: Signed a memorandum of understanding with 25 fellow governors to create the American Governors' Border Strike Force to address the negative impacts of increased illegal immigration on public safety and crime (2022).
items.q: In April 2022, Burgum signed a memorandum of understanding with 25 fellow governors to create the American Governors’ Border Strike Force

items.t: Said the Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade was a victory for North Dakotans who fought to protect the unborn in the state.
items.q: this decision is a victory for the many North Dakotans who have fought so hard and for so long to protect the unborn in our state.

items.t: Said decisions on abortion restrictions should be left to the state.
items.q: Burgum has said decisions on abortion restrictions should be left to the state.

items.t: Said "gargantuan, unreliable, intermittent energy projects hold America back from achieving U.S. Energy Dominance."
items.q: Gargantuan, unreliable, intermittent energy projects hold America back from achieving U.S. Energy Dominance

items.t: Said unleashing America's energy resources will lower prices "at the pump, at the grocery store and across all aspects of American life."
items.q: Unleashing America’s energy resources will lower prices at the pump, at the grocery store and across all aspects of American life

items.t: Supports the Dakota Access Pipeline, describing it as an essential part of North Dakota's and the nation's energy infrastructure.
items.q: DAPL is an essential part of North Dakota's and the nation's energy infrastructure. It plays a pivotal role in ensuring energy security and affordability for the entire nation while providing enormous positive economic impact that touches every North Dakota citizen.

items.t: Announced a goal for North Dakota to become carbon neutral by 2030, to be achieved through significant CCS implementation.
items.q: Governor Doug Burgum announced a goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2030 while retaining the core position of its fossil fuel industries, and to do so by significant CCS implementation.

items.t: Signed HB1398, which requires the teaching of computer science and cybersecurity in school coursework from kindergarten through 12th grade.
items.q: Gov. Doug Burgum and North Dakota School Superintendent Kirsten Baesler on Friday celebrated the governor’s signing of HB1398, which requires the teaching of computer science and cybersecurity and the integration of these content standards into school coursework from kindergarten through 12th grade.

items.t: Said the attack by Hamas terrorists on Israel is reprehensible and despicable, and said North Dakota stands with Israel (2023).
items.q: The attack by Hamas terrorists on Israel is reprehensible, and the fact it occurred on a Jewish holiday is despicable. We stand with our democratic ally Israel

items.t: Blamed Iran, which he said funds and trains Hamas, for the Hamas attacks on Israel.
items.q: Hamas terrorists launched attacks over the weekend. Burgum placed blame in several places. First on Iran which funds and trains Hamas.

items.t: Announced, together with HUD Secretary Scott Turner, a Joint Task Force on Federal Land for Housing to identify underutilized federal lands suitable for residential development and promote policies that increase the availability of affordable housing.
items.q: U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) Secretary Doug Burgum announced a Joint Task Force on Federal Land for Housing to identify underutilized federal lands suitable for residential development, streamline land transfer processes and promote policies that increase the availability of affordable housing.

items.t: Said his grazing order "cuts through bureaucratic red tape to deliver certainty and flexibility for our nation’s ranchers."
items.q: This order cuts through bureaucratic red tape to deliver certainty and flexibility for our nation’s ranchers

record.t: Signed a Secretary's Order to expand livestock grazing on federal rangelands and cut red tape for ranchers, implementing President Trump's "Supporting America's Ranchers" order.
record.q: Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum today signed a Secretary’s Order to expand grazing opportunities, improve the health of federal rangelands

record.t: Signed a Secretary's Order requiring Interior to weigh an energy project's "capacity density" when permitting projects such as wind and solar on federal land.
record.q: the Department will now consider proposed energy project’s capacity density

record.t: Transferred about 109,651 acres of federal land along the U.S.-Mexico border in New Mexico to the Army for three years to support Border Patrol operations.
record.q: announce the emergency withdrawal and transfer of administrative jurisdiction over approximately 109,651 acres of federal land along the U.S.-Mexico border

record.t: Ordered a halt to all construction activities on the Empire Wind wind farm project off the coast of Long Island, New York.
record.q: Doug Burgum, the interior secretary, called for the cessation of “all construction activities” on the Empire Wind project, which was designed to provide enough electricity to power about 500,000 homes in New York.

record.t: Was announced as nominee for U.S. Secretary of the Interior and chairman of the newly formed National Energy Council.
record.q: President-elect Donald Trump today officially announced that he has nominated North Dakota Gov. Doug Burgum to serve as U.S. Secretary of the Interior and chairman of the newly formed National Energy Council.

record.t: Was named Chair of the new National Energy Dominance Council by President Trump's Executive Order 14213.
record.q: The Secretary of the Interior shall serve as Chair of the Council

record.t: Signed six Secretary's Orders on his first day in office to advance President Trump's energy agenda, including Order 3417 on the national energy emergency.
record.q: signing six Secretary's Orders to make America Energy Dominant

record.t: Was confirmed by the Senate as Secretary of the Interior by a vote of 80-17.
record.q: Douglas Burgum, of North Dakota, to be Secretary of the Interior Vote Counts: YEAs 80 NAYs 17

record.t: Directed the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management to hold the next scheduled oil and gas lease sale in the Gulf of America.
record.q: Doug Burgum has directed the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management to hold the next scheduled oil and gas lease sale in the Gulf of America

record.t: Appointed Tammy Miller as North Dakota lieutenant governor after Brent Sanford announced his resignation.

record.t: Signed a $515 million tax relief package that includes House Bill 1158, providing $358 million in income tax relief and $157 million in property tax relief.
record.q: Working with lawmakers, on April 27 Burgum signed a $515 million tax relief package that will provide $358 million in income tax relief

record.t: Signed HB1398, which requires the teaching of computer science and cybersecurity in school coursework from kindergarten through 12th grade.
record.q: Gov. Doug Burgum and North Dakota School Superintendent Kirsten Baesler on Friday celebrated the governor’s signing of HB1398, which requires the teaching of computer science and cybersecurity and the integration of these content standards into school coursework from kindergarten through 12th grade.

record.t: Signed into law a bill banning the teaching of Critical Race Theory in North Dakota public schools.
record.q: On Friday, the North Dakota state Senate passed a bill banning the teaching of Critical Race Theory in public schools; the state House of Representatives passed the bill the day before. On Friday, Republican Governor Doug Burgum signed the bill into law.
